hunks.baseline: Along with that grisly tearing sound, a sensation I had experienced hundreds—thousands—of times traveled through my fingertips.
hunks.sol: The grisly sound came with a sensation I had felt hundreds—thousands—of times before, traveling up through my fingertips.

hunks.baseline: The feeling of flesh splitting and bones breaking.
hunks.sol: Flesh splitting. Bone breaking.

hunks.baseline: It was a sensation I had grown used to at some point, and one that occasionally left a bitter taste in my mouth.
Because becoming accustomed to something like this meant I had taken that many lives with my own hands.
hunks.sol: Somewhere along the way, I had grown used to it. Sometimes that left a bitter taste in my mouth. Being used to it meant I had taken that many lives with my own hands.

hunks.baseline: But at least this time, things were different. As I looked down at the dying man, I felt not the slightest trace of bitterness.
hunks.sol: But not this time. As I looked down at the dying man, I felt no bitterness at all.

hunks.baseline: “Urgh……!”
A final groan escaped with a deflating sound. At the same time, the solidly built man dropped to his knees.
hunks.sol: A final gasp escaped him like air from a punctured tire, and the solidly built man dropped to his knees.

hunks.baseline: The blood-red glow in his eyes, once terrifying enough to make anyone flinch, gradually faded. His entire body trembled faintly before the death rushing toward him.
hunks.sol: The blood-red glow in his eyes, once chilling to look at, slowly faded. His whole body trembled before the death closing in on him.

hunks.baseline: No—perhaps what the man, Go Jun, feared was not death itself, but me, the one who had sentenced him to it.
hunks.sol: No. Perhaps it wasn’t death itself that Go Jun feared. Perhaps it was me, the one who had dealt it to him.

hunks.baseline: His voice and eyes seemed ready to go out at any moment.
hunks.sol: His voice was fading, and so was the light in his eyes. I felt no pity.

Because my opponent wasn’t human like me. He was a monster.

hunks.sol: The Peace Guild had lost Kim Hwajong today. Thousands of people whose names I would never know had lost family and friends they loved. For the madness Go Jun had caused, this death almost seemed too easy.

hunks.baseline: For the price of committing such madness, his death felt almost too easy. It was unfair.
I looked down coldly at Go Jun, who was convulsing in pain on his knees.
hunks.sol: I looked down coldly at him as he knelt there, convulsing in pain.

hunks.baseline: That was the end.

hunks.sol: That was the end. His face fell into a pool of his own blood, and he stopped moving, eyes still wide open.

hunks.baseline: As I looked down at the corpse of the monster, no breath or spark of life remaining, I suddenly realized it.
hunks.sol: As I looked at the monster’s corpse, with no breath or trace of life left in it, a thought came to me.

hunks.baseline: The Disciple who had served Lee Jungryong faithfully for decades—and the de facto master of Ares Guild, one of the foremost Guilds in the world—had died by my hand.
hunks.sol: Lee Jungryong’s loyal Disciple of several decades—the man who had effectively ruled Ares Guild, one of the foremost Guilds in the world—had died by my hand.

hunks.baseline: He had caused two Monster Waves on purpose, creating thousands of casualties and costing Kim Hwajong and some twenty members of the Peace Guild their lives.
hunks.sol: He had deliberately caused two Monster Waves, leaving thousands dead or injured and costing Kim Hwajong and some twenty Peace Guild members their lives. He had paid for it with his own.

hunks.baseline: He had paid for it with his life.
*So this really is the end……*
hunks.sol: *So this really is the end…*

hunks.baseline: But why?
Why did my heart feel hollow even after my revenge was complete? It was as though the hole was not in Go Jun’s chest, but in mine.
hunks.sol: Then why did I feel so hollow? I had taken my revenge, yet it felt as though the hole was in my chest, not Go Jun’s.

hunks.baseline: It was probably because I knew that the people who had left my side would never return.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was because I knew the people who had left us would never come back.

hunks.baseline: I turned away, asking questions that would never reach them.
hunks.sol: I turned away, asking questions that could never reach them.

hunks.baseline: Resisting fatigue and drowsiness heavy enough to crush my entire body, I slowly crossed the dark corridor, devastated by the fierce battle.
hunks.sol: Fatigue and drowsiness weighed on me more heavily than I could have imagined. I fought them off and slowly crossed the dark corridor, wrecked by our battle.

hunks.baseline: With every step, faces and memories rose before my eyes and obscured my vision.
hunks.sol: With every step, faces and memories rose before my eyes.

hunks.baseline: I saw Gwangan Bridge collapsing and heard the screams of people consumed by terror. In the family photograph hanging from the rearview mirror of a passenger car, I remembered a promise I had made long ago by linking my pinky with someone I missed more than words could say.
hunks.sol: I saw Gwangan Bridge collapsing. I heard people screaming in terror. A family photograph dangling from a car’s rearview mirror brought back a promise I had made long ago, pinkies linked with someone I missed more than words could say.

hunks.baseline: “When Hayeon gets a little older, and you, Taekyung, start middle school, let’s come see the sea again. All right?”
hunks.sol: “When Hayeon’s a little older, and you start middle school, Taekyung, we’ll come back to see the sea. Okay?”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. Here, promise.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. Come on, pinky promise.”

hunks.baseline: But today, the place from the promise I had kept deep in my heart had collapsed.
hunks.sol: But today, the place I had kept with that promise deep in my heart had collapsed.

hunks.baseline: Innocent people had died, and monsters had spread like a plague. I had done everything I could, but I had failed to save more lives.
hunks.sol: Innocent people had died, and monsters had spread like a plague. I had done everything I could, but I hadn’t saved more of them.

hunks.baseline: My heart was just as unsteady as my staggering footsteps. Amid that confusion, a warm voice rang out in my mind.
hunks.sol: My thoughts were as unsteady as my feet. Through the confusion, a warm voice echoed in my mind.

hunks.baseline: The silver-haired old butler who had comforted me even as he died had departed on a journey from which he could not return.
hunks.sol: The graying old butler who had comforted me even as he died had gone somewhere he could never return from.

hunks.baseline: Whether the world he had reached was night or day. Whether it was cold or warm. I had no way of knowing.
I could only hope.
That his world was at least a little brighter. That he, who had trembled in the cold, was somewhere warmer.
hunks.sol: I had no way of knowing whether it was night or day where he had arrived. Whether it was cold or warm. I could only hope that his world was a little brighter. That he, who had shivered in the cold, was somewhere warmer.

hunks.baseline: And…… that he had believed my lie to the very end—the lie that the person he had wanted to see one last time had come.
hunks.sol: And… that he had believed my lie to the very end—the lie that the person he had wanted to see one last time had come.

hunks.baseline: Nothing happens without consequences. I believed someone had to pay the price. I believed that being punished for doing wrong was only natural.
hunks.sol: Every action had an outcome. Someone had to pay the price. I had believed it was only natural for a person who did wrong to be punished.

hunks.baseline: That was why I had come here. I had thrown open the gates of a palace no one had dared approach and brought down an impregnable fortress.
hunks.sol: That was why I had come here. I had thrown open the gates of a palace no one could touch and brought down an impregnable fortress.

hunks.baseline: I had fought, and fought, and fought again. And after finally killing the monster wearing a human face, I suddenly felt hollow inside and found myself wondering:
hunks.sol: I had fought, and fought, and fought again. But after finally killing the monster wearing a human skin, I felt a sudden emptiness in my chest. One question came to mind.

hunks.baseline: I had thought that if I killed Go Jun, the root of all this evil, at least some of my anger would disappear. I thought I might even laugh out loud in relief.
hunks.sol: I had thought that killing Go Jun, the cause of it all, would ease my anger, even a little. I had thought I might laugh out loud with relief.

hunks.baseline: But I hadn’t.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: I could create and fill a massive pit with a single gesture, yet I could not fill the emptiness in my heart.
hunks.sol: With one gesture, I could make a massive pit and fill it again. But I couldn’t fill the empty place in my heart.

hunks.baseline: It had been the same three years ago, and it was the same now.
hunks.sol: It had been the same three years ago. It was the same now.

hunks.baseline: My mouth tasted bitter.
In the end, enduring the wounds was left entirely to those who remained.
hunks.sol: My mouth tasted bitter. In the end, the wounds were left for those of us still here to bear.

hunks.baseline: I even found myself regretting that I might have given Go Jun a death that was too painless……
hunks.sol: I almost regretted giving Go Jun such a painless death.

hunks.baseline: I suddenly stopped walking.
hunks.sol: I stopped.

hunks.baseline: By then, an inexplicable sense of wrongness had seized my entire body. A cold chill slowly crawled up my spine.
hunks.sol: At some point, an inexplicable sense that something was wrong had taken hold of me. A chill crept up my spine.

hunks.baseline: Was it because of my extreme fatigue? Or perhaps because of my complicated emotions? My mind was hazy, shrouded in fog.
hunks.sol: Was it the exhaustion? Or everything weighing on my mind? My thoughts were as murky as fog.

hunks.baseline: But after standing motionless and thinking for a moment, I finally realized the source of that wrongness.
hunks.sol: I stood there for a moment. Then I realized what was wrong.

hunks.baseline: *Go Jun should definitely be dead. So why……*
hunks.sol: *Go Jun should be dead. So why…*

hunks.baseline: Why had the System window announcing his kill still not appeared?
hunks.sol: Why hadn’t the System window announcing the kill appeared?

hunks.baseline: I had driven a spearhead into the center of his chest and burned his organs. I had watched and felt him stop breathing with my own eyes.
hunks.sol: I had driven my spearhead into the center of his chest and burned his organs. I had seen his face fall into that pool of blood and felt his breathing stop.

hunks.baseline: I muttered under my breath and turned around.
The corridor, horribly destroyed by the fierce battle, was shrouded in unusually deep darkness.
hunks.sol: I muttered the words and turned around. An unusually deep darkness had settled over the ruined corridor.

hunks.baseline: The System was absolute and immediate.
hunks.sol: The System was absolute, and it was immediate.

hunks.baseline: I knew that better than anyone. I simply had not noticed anything strange because I had been overwhelmed by exhaustion and deep thoughts in the moment of victory.
hunks.sol: I knew that better than anyone. Exhaustion and the thoughts that had consumed me after my apparent victory had kept me from noticing sooner.

hunks.baseline: That was why I was not terribly surprised when I saw that the puddle of blood where Go Jun had been lying was empty.
hunks.sol: So when I found the pool of blood empty, I was not especially surprised.

hunks.baseline: The man who looked so completely different from the last time I had seen him.

hunks.sol: My quiet voice echoed down the corridor. Go Jun—or rather, the *monster*—turned as he staggered along.

hunks.sol: “Jin… Taekyung. Karruk.”

hunks.baseline: “Shut…… up. This…… this wasn’t what I wanted either—”

hunks.sol: I did not wait for an answer. Without a moment’s hesitation, I brought the transparent spearhead down.

hunks.baseline: With a sharp cutting sound, the head separated from the body and rolled across the ground.
hunks.sol: His head came free with a sharp cutting sound and rolled across the floor.

hunks.baseline: That was the end of the monster who had become neither a hero like Cheon Taemin nor an ambitious warlord like his Master, Lee Jungryong.
hunks.sol: That was the end of a monster who had become neither a hero like Cheon Taemin nor an ambitious warlord like his Master, Lee Jungryong.

hunks.baseline: Along with the familiar chime piercing my ears, I picked up Go Jun’s head from the puddle of blood.
hunks.sol: The familiar chime rang in my ears. I picked up Go Jun’s head from the pool of blood and crossed the space where I alone remained, my steps slow and unsteady.

hunks.baseline: Then, with slow, staggering steps, I crossed the space where I alone remained.
